---
title: "Sensitivity to the prior standard deviation"
subtitle: "1.6 · the prior SD of a teaching posterior, after Walters' teaching slides"
description: "Repeated-sampling squared error and pairwise posterior probabilities across prior standard deviations."
---

Varying the prior standard deviation from .01 to 1 across the [simulated league](shrinkage.qmd) shows that posterior means minimize squared error near the true spread while reshaping [pairwise posterior probabilities](two-units.qmd).

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Near the true spread.** At prior SD .15 (true spread .149), mean squared error hits its grid minimum in this draw (.00958 vs. .0163 for estimates) and expected (.00754 vs. .0175; fine grid .146).
- **Much too narrow.** At .02, overshrinking raises squared error above the estimates (.0197 vs. .0163 in this draw; .0191 vs. .0175 expected), and only 6 of the 435 pairs exceed .90.
- **Too narrow.** At .05, squared error rises to .0148 (.0133 expected), expected misordered pairs reach 87.4, and 17 of 30 units end farther from truth.
- **Too wide.** At .45, expected squared error matches .05 at .0133 (.0136 in this draw), yet 159 of the 435 pairs exceed .90 (45 exceed .99) and 13 units end farther.
- **Another draw.** Under seed 20261031, this draw's minimum moves to .12 (.00917), while expected squared error stays lowest at .15 (.00754).

<details>
<summary>Fixed-parameter experiment and source notes</summary>

The dashed curve ("expected") gives the closed-form expected squared error across repeated estimate draws with the true values fixed — a fixed-parameter experiment in the postrank theory book (ch. 24, "Hyperparameters, precision and represented uncertainty"). postrank fits no model and takes the posterior it is given as input; whether high-probability directions hold under the true values is examined in [Reported error and reference-law evaluation](../grades/reported-and-realized.qmd). Normal–normal shrinkage follows Walters' Mixtape slides (p. 27).

</details>
